cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What does macOS Gatekeeper check before letting downloaded software run?
cards.answer: That the code carries a signature from an identified Apple Developer ID, has been notarized by Apple's automated malware scan, and has not been altered since signing.

cards.heading: Trigger mechanism
cards.question: What triggers Gatekeeper's check on a downloaded file?
cards.answer: The quarantine attribute macOS attaches to any file that arrived over the network.

cards.heading: Default policy
cards.question: What happens by default when software fails Gatekeeper's signature or notarization check?
cards.answer: It is blocked or flagged with a generic, alarming warning on first launch that most users will not click through.

cards.heading: Notarization vs App Store review
cards.question: Is Apple notarization the same as full App Store review?
cards.answer: No — notarization is Apple's automated scan for known malicious content, not full App Store review.

cards.heading: Randomized launch locations
cards.question: Why does Gatekeeper open apps from randomized read-only locations?
cards.answer: So a malicious plug-in bundled with a legitimate app cannot load unnoticed.
